claims.text: A machine-learning-based potential, such as a neural-network potential, can better represent the many atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is to implement a machine-learning-based potential as the thermodynamic-integration reference.
The intervention is intended to apply to both solid and liquid alloy states at or near their high melting temperatures.
Improved representation of atomic configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learning reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is near and above the alloys' melting points.
Elemental or binary calculations provide supporting evidence for the proposed use of machine-learning potentials.
There is no direct cited evidence for the intervention in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
